title: How to lace cross-stitch onto mount card
subtitle: Stretching and securing the finished piece for display or framing
excerpt: Lacing is the traditional method of mounting a finished cross-stitch piece onto stiff card for display or framing. The fabric is pulled evenly over the card and stitched at the back with lacing thread, giving a taut, flat surface without any adhesive that might deteriorate or stain the piece over time.
sourceNotes: Traditional needlework mounting technique. Documented in Weldon's Practical Needlework series (1880s), Internet Archive. Standard technique in cross-stitch publisher guides.

glossaryTerms.definition: A stiff, evenly-woven cross-stitch fabric with clearly visible squares formed by groups of threads.

content.text: Lacing a cross-stitch piece onto mount card is the preferred finish before framing. The fabric wraps around a piece of stiff acid-free card cut to the finished size, and lacing thread sewn across the back holds it under even tension. The result is flat and taut with no adhesive involved, and the piece can be unlaced and re-mounted years later without damage.

Cut mount card to the finished design size. Acid-free mount board is recommended; standard card will work for display purposes but may yellow the fabric over many years. Make sure the card dimensions match the stitched area exactly.
face-down on a clean surface. Centre the card over it, stitched side against the card, with at least 3 cm of fabric border on each side.

Fold the top and bottom fabric margins over the back of the card. Insert pins into the card edge to hold the fabric temporarily while you work. Pull the top and bottom margins taut so the fabric is flat against the front of the card with no slack, but not so tight that it distorts the weave.

Thread a large-eye needle with strong linen thread or crochet cotton. Starting at the top, take long stitches back and forth across the back of the card from top margin to bottom margin, zigzagging like laces. Work from the centre outward so the tension stays even.

Remove the temporary pins from the top and bottom and fold in the left and right margins, mitring the corners neatly. Lace across the left and right margins in the same way. Pull gently on each lacing pass to keep the tension even and the fabric smooth across the front.

Turn the piece over and check from the front. The stitched design should sit centred on the card, the fabric flat and even, with no pulled threads or diagonal puckers. Corners should be mitre-folded neatly.

items.symptom: The design is not centred on the card
items.cause: The fabric was not centred before folding.
items.fix: Unfold, reposition the card under the fabric so the design is centred, and begin again from step 2. Check the centering by measuring from the outer edge of the stitched border to the fabric border on all four sides.

items.symptom: The lacing thread pulls the corners inward and makes the edges bow
items.cause: Too much tension on the lacing, or the mitre folds were too bulky.
items.fix: Reduce the tension on the lacing passes. Trim the mitre fold at the corners to reduce bulk before folding; a thin fold creates a flatter corner.

content.text: A laced piece drops straight into a frame without any extra materials. Take the laced piece to a framer or fit it into a standard frame with a pre-cut mount. The back is as clean as the front.
